_comment: Trail events. Pools: config common_events (anywhere), each region's events list, and a side quest's theme list (quests.json events). Each option may have requires {item, money, hides, skill (survival), class, quirk} and consume {item: n, money: n, hides: n}. The hero who meets a skill/class/quirk requirement is the actor ({hero}); options needing a skill, class or quirk are hidden without it. compel: true on a quirk option = 30% (event_compel_chance) the hero takes it before the company chooses. experts {class|skill|quirk id: {odds, averse, bonus, always, swap, add, free, fight}} = the curio expert rules over the whole company (★/✗ shown by name). Outcomes are weighted; experts shrink (or, averse, grow) the non-good outcomes; effects use the shared effect format.

river_crossing.title: River Crossing
river_crossing.text: The trail runs straight into a wide, muddy river. The current looks slow, but the depth is hard to judge.

options.text: Ford it: drive the wagon straight across.

outcomes.text: Water to the wagon beds, but you make it across.
The wagon tips in the current! Supplies wash away and everyone is soaked.
{hero} is swept off their feet and dragged downstream before the others haul them out.

options.text: Caulk the wagon and float it across.

outcomes.text: {hero} seals every seam with pitch. The wagon floats like a riverboat.
{hero} reads the ripples and finds the shallows. You also catch dinner on the way.
The ferryman poles you across and tells stories the whole way.

broken_axle.title: Broken Axle
broken_axle.text: A loud crack, and the wagon lurches to one side. The rear axle has split.

outcomes.text: A new axle, a few curses, and you're rolling again.

options.text: Rig a repair from what's on hand.

outcomes.text: {hero} splints the axle with a fence rail. Better than new, almost.
It holds. Barely.
Hours of work in the hot sun.
The repair fails and the wagon drags. The whole day is lost.

prairie_fire.title: Prairie Fire
prairie_fire.text: Smoke on the western horizon, and it's coming fast. The grass is burning, and the wind is at its back.

outcomes.text: You outrun the flames, lungs burning.
The fire catches the wagon canvas before you reach the creek.

options.text: Set a backfire: burn a patch to shelter in.

outcomes.text: {hero} lights a backfire. The blaze splits around your burned patch and roars past.

options.text: Soak the blankets in whiskey and hunker down.

outcomes.text: Whiskey burns too, it turns out. But the wet blankets hold and you're mostly fine.
{hero} blows a firebreak through the sod. The flames lie down and die at its edge.

stranger_on_road.title: Stranger on the Road
stranger_on_road.text: A lone rider sits a tired horse in the middle of the trail. "Evenin'. Mind if I share your fire?"

outcomes.text: The stranger tells you about the trail ahead and leaves at dawn.
The stranger asks to join the company.
You wake to find the stranger gone, and so is some of your money.

options.text: Share a bottle and ask questions.

outcomes.text: The whiskey loosens their tongue. They sketch you a map of the region.
{hero} recognizes a wanted horse thief and brings them in. There's a bounty.
{hero} has the stranger's face folded in a saddlebag. The stranger goes for their iron.

options.text: Drink with the stranger till dawn.

outcomes.text: Somewhere around the third bottle the stranger draws a map on {hero}'s arm.
{hero} wakes with a sore head and a lighter purse. The stranger is long gone.

options.text: Keep your hand on your iron and ride on.

outcomes.text: You pass without a word. The stranger watches you go.

buffalo_herd.title: Buffalo Herd
buffalo_herd.text: The ground trembles. A herd of buffalo darkens the plain from horizon to horizon, and your trail runs right through it.

outcomes.text: It takes most of the day. Everyone is restless and hungry.
{hero} brings down a young cow cleanly. Meat for days, and a hide worth tanning.

options.text: Bring one down and salt the meat.

outcomes.text: One clean shot and a long afternoon with the salt. It'll keep for weeks.
The shot goes wide and the herd thunders off. All that salt for nothing.

1.text: {hero} cuts a yearling out of the herd and the rest part around it. Meat for the pot.

outcomes.text: The herd parts. Mostly.
A bull takes exception to your wagon.

sick_traveler.title: Sick Traveler
sick_traveler.text: A family's wagon sits by the trail. The father is burning with fever. "Please. Anything you can spare."

outcomes.text: The fever breaks by morning. They press a trinket on you and refuse to take it back.
{hero} works through the night. The father lives. The family sings your names as you leave.
{hero} works through the night and the father lives. Come spring, the family says, they'll look for your town: "Folks like you are folks worth living near."
It isn't much, but it's something. You feel good about it.
{hero} prays with them through the night. Whatever happens, they aren't alone.
By morning the fever breaks. The mother presses a keepsake into {hero}'s hands.
{hero} finds the fang marks under the bandage. One dose and the man is sitting up by noon.

options.text: Keep moving. You can't risk the sickness.

outcomes.text: Nobody talks for the next few miles.

rattler_in_bedroll.title: Rattler in the Bedroll
rattler_in_bedroll.text: {hero} goes to lie down and hears the dry buzz of a rattlesnake coiled in their blankets.

options.text: Freeze, and let someone else deal with it.

0.text: {hero} pins it and milks the venom into a vial. Handy stuff.

outcomes.text: A quick shovel stroke and it's over.
It strikes before anyone gets there.
{hero} snatches it up like a garden hose. Snake for supper.

options.text: Keep Antivenom handy and swat it.

outcomes.text: It bites anyway, but the antivenom works.
{hero} is fifty yards off before anyone else moves. By the time they creep back, the snake's been dealt with.

thunderstorm.title: Thunderstorm
thunderstorm.text: Black clouds pile up out of nowhere. Hail the size of marbles starts to fall.

add.text: Lightning hits the wagon tongue right beside {hero}. Hair on end, singed, and humming with it.

outcomes.text: A miserable, soaking night. The powder's damp.
Lightning spooks the oxen and they drag the wagon into a ditch.

options.text: Tell stories to pass the time.

outcomes.text: {hero}'s ghost stories have everyone laughing by midnight.
Not so bad after a few swallows.

lost_trail.title: Lost the Trail
lost_trail.text: The ruts you've been following just... end. Tall grass in every direction.

outcomes.text: You find the trail again by noon.
A whole day wasted wandering.
{hero} finds the old wheel ruts under the grass, and a shortcut besides.
{hero} rides to a ridge and spots the trail, and more.

wolf_tracks.title: Wolf Tracks
wolf_tracks.text: Big paw prints circle the camp. They were here last night, watching.

outcomes.text: {hero}'s traps catch two wolves. Prime pelts, and a bounty besides.

options.text: Hunt them down before they hunt you.

outcomes.text: You find them. Or they find you.

options.text: Keep a big fire going and move on.

outcomes.text: Nobody sleeps much.
The wolves try their luck anyway.

options.text: Go out and meet the pack.

outcomes.text: {hero} sits in the dark until the pack comes. They sniff, and leave a fresh kill behind as they go.
One young wolf doesn't listen.
{hero} doctors a strip of meat. By morning, two wolves lie stiff by the trail.

abandoned_homestead.title: Abandoned Homestead
abandoned_homestead.text: A sod house, door hanging open. A table still set for supper, the plates coated in dust.

outcomes.text: Canned goods in the root cellar.

then.text: Behind the shelves: a cellar door with a fresh padlock. Somebody's been here, and not long ago.

outcomes.text: Somebody's stash: a keepsake and a roll of chips.
Somebody's stash, and the somebodies come home.
Not your business. Probably wise.
Somebody else has already claimed the place.
Something about the place is wrong. Nobody wants to stay.

options.text: Tear down the barn for lumber.

outcomes.text: Good seasoned boards.
{hero} lights a short fuse. When the dust settles: a strongbox and a crate of nails.
The blast brings the squatters running, ears ringing.

options.text: Light a lamp and search properly.

outcomes.text: By lamplight the cellar gives up its shelves, and a little more.

options.text: Open the door nobody wants to open.

outcomes.text: Behind it: a child's room, untouched, and a silver locket on the pillow.
Behind it: the family. What's left of them gets up.
Some places are better left alone.

haint_lights.title: Haint Lights
haint_lights.text: Pale green lights bob in the tall grass after sundown, drifting closer, then away. Almost like they want to be followed.

outcomes.text: The lights lead you off the trail and stop, hovering, over a lone grave.

then.text: The lights hang over the grave, waiting. The marker's name has worn away.

outcomes.text: Under the coffin lid: someone's buried savings, wrapped in oilcloth.
The haint rises out of the hole after you.

options.text: Leave a coin on the marker (10 chips).

outcomes.text: One by one the lights go out. {hero} feels watched over.
The lights don't follow.
They lead you in circles until dawn, and then they turn and come for you.
The lights circle all night but never cross the salt. By morning they've gone.
{hero} reads from Ecclesiastes until the lights go out one by one.

options.text: Light your own lamp and follow.

outcomes.text: The lights shy from the lamp and lead you, sullen, to someone's buried savings.
The lamp gutters out, and the lights close in.

options.text: Chase the lights alone. There's gold out there.

outcomes.text: {hero} comes back at dawn with mud to the elbows and a sack of old coins.
{hero} comes back screaming, and the lights come with them.

peddler.title: Traveling Peddler
peddler.text: A painted wagon rattles up. "Tonics! Tinctures! Rope, nails, and genuine lucky charms!"

outcomes.text: It seems genuine enough.
It's a painted rock.
Bandages and a bottle of something.
{hero} wins the peddler's stock in a hand of poker.
{hero} sniffs, sips and nods. Some of it's the real thing.
Snake oil, every bottle. The peddler pays {hero} to keep it quiet.

options.text: Buy his whole case of rotgut (60 chips).

outcomes.text: {hero} cracks the first bottle before the chips change hands. A fine evening, and a rough morning.
The peddler shrugs and rattles on.

trinket_peddler.title: The Trinket Peddler
trinket_peddler.text: A tiny woman on a mule, her coat sewn all over with little pockets. "Charms, tokens, keepsakes of the famous dead. Every one of 'em lucky, or your chips back." She has never once given anyone their chips back.

options.text: Buy something from the top pocket (90 chips).

outcomes.text: She presses it into your hand and closes your fingers over it.

options.text: Ask about the inside pocket (260 chips).

outcomes.text: She glances both ways before she shows you. It's the real thing.
It's a nice rock. A very nice rock. She's already riding away.
{hero} tells her fortune so well she pays in trinkets.
"Your loss, pilgrim."

wagon_stuck.title: Stuck in the Mud
wagon_stuck.text: The wagon sinks to its hubs in a slough. The oxen strain and bawl.

0.text: {hero} gets a shoulder under the axle and lifts the wagon clean out. Everyone stares.

outcomes.text: Muddy, exhausted, but free.
Somebody wrenches their back.
Block and tackle does the work of ten men.
{hero} cuts saplings for a corduroy road. Out in no time.

gravesite.title: Row of Graves
gravesite.text: Six fresh graves beside the trail. Cholera, says the scrawled board. Keep moving.

0.text: {hero} says a few words over each grave. It helps.

outcomes.text: A solemn moment. It hits some harder than others.
{hero}'s service brings the company some peace.

options.text: Dig one up. They won't miss it.

outcomes.text: A wedding ring and a pocket watch. {hero} doesn't look anyone in the eye.
Cholera doesn't stay buried. {hero} is burning up by nightfall, and nobody wants to sit near them.
Nobody looks at the graves.

hunting_grounds.title: Good Hunting
hunting_grounds.text: Fresh game sign everywhere: pronghorn, deer and turkey. A chance to stock up.

outcomes.text: A fat pronghorn!
Nothing but sore feet.
{hero} comes back with more meat than you can carry.
{hero} finds roots, greens and a snared rabbit.

outlaw_ambush_warning.title: Smoke Signals
outlaw_ambush_warning.text: Thin columns of smoke on a ridge ahead. Outlaws, signaling each other. They know you're coming.

options.text: Ride hard and hit them first.

outcomes.text: You catch them off guard!
{hero} leads you on a deer trail around the ambush. You even spot their stash.
{hero} drops the lookout from three hundred yards. The rest come on half-blind.
{hero} rolls a lit bundle down onto their camp. They come out of the smoke staggering.
Safe, but it costs you a day.

options.text: Charge in before the plan's made.

outcomes.text: {hero} is already riding at them, hollering. The outlaws have all the time in the world to aim.

fork_in_trail.title: Fork in the Trail
fork_in_trail.text: A weathered sign: 'SHORTCUT' points left toward rough hills; the main trail curves right.

outcomes.text: It really is shorter.
Rough ground. The wagon takes a beating.
Slow and steady.
Heads. {hero} grins: it really is shorter.
Tails. Rough ground, and the wagon takes a beating.

flash_flood.title: Flash Flood
flash_flood.text: A roar echoes up the dry wash. A wall of brown water is coming down the canyon.

outcomes.text: Everyone makes it, but the wagon is battered.
{hero} is caught by the water and pulled out half-drowned.

options.text: Haul the wagon up with rope.

outcomes.text: You winch the wagon up the cliff just in time.
{hero} had you camp high last night. The flood passes harmlessly below.

railroad_survey.title: Railroad Surveyors
railroad_survey.text: Men with transits and chains are staking out a rail line, right through a settler's orchard. The railroad men carry rifles.

outcomes.text: The settler watches you leave.
The company men don't run.
{hero} points out that their stakes are on a homestead claim. The surveyors grumble and move the line. The settler gives you supplies.
The surveyors move their line. The settler looks at the stakes, then at the orchard. "They'll be back. I'd sooner start over somewhere with law in it." They ask the way to your town.

siren_song.title: A Song in the Canyon
siren_song.text: A woman's voice echoes down the canyon, beautiful and aching. Everyone feels the pull to go find the singer.

options.text: Stuff your ears with wax and push on.

outcomes.text: The song fades behind you.
{hero} pulls the wax out and runs toward the voice. You chase them down.

options.text: Tie everyone to the wagon, like the old story.

outcomes.text: Everyone struggles and weeps, but the ropes hold. At dawn, a nest of treasure lies abandoned on the ledge.

options.text: Answer the song with a louder one.

outcomes.text: {hero} bellows every trail song they know. The siren goes quiet, offended.

heat_wave.title: Heat Wave
heat_wave.text: The sun hammers down. The water barrel is low, and the oxen are foaming.

outcomes.text: Slow, but cooler.
Brutal. Everyone suffers.
{hero} follows the cottonwoods to a hidden spring.

claim_dispute.title: Claim Dispute
claim_dispute.text: Two prospectors are shouting over a stake, guns half drawn. "Tell him! This here's MY claim!"

outcomes.text: {hero} reads the claim papers and settles it. Both pay a finder's fee to keep it official.
{hero} settles it by the papers. The loser spits, then shrugs: "Reckon I'd rather draw wages than dig for nothing. Your town got a mine?"
{hero} points out the real vein is twenty yards over. Both are grateful.
{hero} sets a charge between the stakes. The ore shows which claim is which, and both men pay for the answer.
{hero}'s shot takes the hat off the louder one. Both men decide to sort it out at the land office.
Gunshots behind you as you leave.
They both decide YOU'RE the claim jumpers.

avalanche.title: Avalanche!
avalanche.text: A crack like a rifle shot from the peaks above, and the whole snowfield starts to slide.

outcomes.text: You make it, barely. The wagon is half buried.
{hero} is buried and dug out blue.

options.text: The Scout picked the safe line.

outcomes.text: {hero} kept you under the rock overhang. The snow thunders past.

blizzard.title: Blizzard
blizzard.text: White out. You can't see the oxen in front of the wagon.

outcomes.text: Two days of cold and short rations.
{hero} keeps a roaring fire going all night.
Frostbite and misery, but you make progress.

frozen_traveler.title: Frozen Traveler
frozen_traveler.text: A figure sits by a dead fire, covered in frost. Alive. Barely.

options.text: Warm them up and bring them along.

outcomes.text: They thaw out, grateful, and offer to join the company.
They don't make it through the night.
Some food and a coin purse. Nobody feels good about it.

giant_footprints.title: Giant Footprints
giant_footprints.text: Footprints in the snow, each one big enough to bathe in. They lead up toward the pass.

outcomes.text: They lead to a young stone giant, and it's not happy.
They lead to a giant's cache of shiny things.
{hero} works out where the giants walk, and how to avoid them.
A sensible choice.

homestead_family.title: Homestead
homestead_family.text: A sod house with smoke curling from the chimney. A family waves you in. "We don't get many visitors!"

outcomes.text: Fresh bread, butter and a real bed. Everyone rests easy.
Sacks of potatoes and salt pork.

options.text: Help with chores in exchange for lumber.

outcomes.text: A day of hard work, a wagon full of boards.
A day of hard work, a wagon full of boards, and the eldest asking if your town needs a strong back.

homestead_widow.title: Widow's Claim
homestead_widow.text: A widow works a claim alone with a shotgun across her knees. "Wolves took my husband. I aim to see them pay."

options.text: Help her clear the wolf den.

outcomes.text: The den is nearby, and occupied.
She's good company. Everyone rests.

options.text: Offer her a place in the company.

outcomes.text: "Reckon there's nothing left for me here." She shoulders her shotgun.
"This is my land. I'm staying."
{hero} spends an afternoon with her and a row of bottles. By sundown she's hitting most of them, and she's packing.

homestead_drifter.title: Drifter's Camp
homestead_drifter.text: A drifter cooking beans over a small fire looks up. "Heading west? Me too, if you'll have me."

outcomes.text: Another hand for the trail.

options.text: Share a meal and move on.

outcomes.text: Good beans. Good company.
{hero} and the drifter trade chalk marks and gossip. They know the trail ahead, and they want in.

homestead_trapper_cabin.title: Trapper's Cabin
homestead_trapper_cabin.text: A log cabin buried to the eaves in snow. A grizzled trapper lets you in to the fire.

outcomes.text: Warm at last.
Furs, pemmican and good advice.

options.text: Ask the trapper to join you.

outcomes.text: "Been meaning to see the ocean before I die."
"Too old to ride with gunhands. But I hear your town buys hides." The trapper starts packing up the traps.

swollen_creek.title: Swollen Creek
swollen_creek.text: Last night's rain turned a trickle into a torrent. The banks are slick and the current is quick.

options.text: Rope the wagon to a tree and ease it across.

outcomes.text: Slow going, but the rope holds and nothing is lost.

options.text: Wait for the water to drop.

outcomes.text: A day and a half of waiting and eating into the stores.
The wagon slews sideways and a wheel cracks on the rocks.
Supplies wash off the back of the wagon.
Soaked, but across.

fever_camp.title: Fever in the Camp
fever_camp.text: {hero} wakes up shivering and burning hot. By noon two others are coughing.

options.text: Treat them with bandages and cool water.

outcomes.text: The fever breaks by nightfall.
{hero} isolates the sick and brews willow-bark tea. Everyone pulls through.

options.text: Push on and hope it passes.

outcomes.text: It passes overnight. Mostly.
It doesn't pass quickly.
{hero} gets the worst of it and may never quite shake it.

outlaw_toll.title: Outlaw Toll
outlaw_toll.text: Three riders block the trail, rifles across their saddles. "Road tax. Forty chips, or we take it out of your hide."

outcomes.text: They count the chips twice and ride off laughing.
{hero} names each of them from the wanted posters. They decide the road is free today.
"Badge don't mean much out here."
You call the leader out. The others back their horses off to watch.

options.text: Double or nothing on a hand of cards.

outcomes.text: {hero} lays down a full house. The riders pay up and ride off grumbling.
{hero} lays down two pair. The riders' leader lays down three of a kind.
{hero} reads their names off the posters, and the bounties too. Guns come out.
Guns come out.
{hero} has already drawn. The riders scatter for cover, but {hero} is standing in the open.

torn_canvas.title: Torn Canvas
torn_canvas.text: A gust rips the wagon's canvas open end to end. Dust and grit pour over everything inside.

outcomes.text: Patched and tied down tight.

options.text: Rebuild the bows with spare parts.

outcomes.text: Better than new.
{hero} stitches a fresh hide over the tear. Tight as a drum.
Grit gets into the food and the gear.

card_game.title: Campfire Card Game
card_game.text: Three cowhands at a fire wave you over. "Faro, friend? Penny a point, chips on the side."

options.text: Sit in for a few hands (50 chips).

add.text: {hero} calls one of them a cheat. Guns come out.

outcomes.text: {hero} walks away from the fire a hundred chips heavier.
Cleaned out. The cowhands are very friendly about it.
Coffee, beans and tall tales.
{hero} stays up with the cowhands and the bottle until the stars fade.
{hero} stays up all night and wins the pot.

medicine_show.title: Medicine Show
medicine_show.text: A painted wagon, a brass band of one, and a man in a tall hat: "Doctor Ezekiel's Miracle Elixir! Cures fever, gout, heartbreak and snakebite!"

outcomes.text: Bracing stuff. {hero} feels ten years younger, for an afternoon.
{hero} spends the night behind a bush.
{hero} turns the crowd. They pelt the doctor with his own bottles and pass the hat for the preacher.
The band plays you out of town.

twister.title: Twister
twister.text: The sky goes green. A black funnel walks across the prairie, straight for the wagon.

outcomes.text: Everyone flat in the gully as the roar goes over.
The wagon's caught in the edge of it.

options.text: Tie down the wagon and lie flat.

outcomes.text: The ropes sing but they hold.

then.text: When the roar passes, a farm's strongbox lies split open in the debris. A family's name is painted on the lid.

outcomes.text: Finders keepers. Nobody says much.
{hero} tracks the family to their cellar. They press a keepsake on you, crying.
You never find them. You leave the box at the next homestead.

cattle_drive.title: Cattle Drive
cattle_drive.text: Three hundred longhorns and a trail boss with half the riders he needs. "Pay's fair, if you'll ride drag for a day."

outcomes.text: A long, dusty day. The trail boss pays in cash.
A long, dusty day. At sundown the cook throws down the apron: "Two thousand miles of beans. Point me at your town."
Something spooks the herd. Stampede!

options.text: Cut out a stray for supper.

outcomes.text: One stray, never missed. Steak tonight.
The drovers catch you at it.
The herd takes an hour to pass.

powder_shack.title: The Powder Shack
powder_shack.text: A tin-roofed shack by the tailings, door hanging open. Inside, crates of dynamite sweat in the heat.

outcomes.text: A few sticks to throw. Everyone breathes again.
BOOM.
Nobody argues.

tapping_underground.title: Tapping Underground
tapping_underground.text: Faint tapping from under a collapsed adit: three knocks, a pause, three more. Someone's alive down there.

outcomes.text: A half-starved miner crawls out into the light. "I owe you. I'll ride with you, if you'll have me."
A miner crawls out, coughing dust. "I'm done with company mines. If your town's got honest work, count me in."
A miner crawls out, and presses his poke into {hero}'s hands.
The roof comes down on {hero}.

options.text: Mark the spot and move on.

outcomes.text: The tapping follows you for a long while.

tommyknockers.title: Tommyknockers
tommyknockers.text: Knocking from the dark of the mine mouth. The old Cornish miners always left the Knockers a bite of supper, for luck.

outcomes.text: By morning the pasty's gone, and two lumps of ore sit on the doorstep.
Nothing happens. Probably.
A rock falls from nowhere. Then the knocking gets closer.
The knocking stops when you've gone.

runaway_burro.title: Runaway Burro
runaway_burro.text: A burro wanders up to the wagon, packed with a prospector's kit: pick, pan, a coil of fuse. No prospector.

outcomes.text: Nobody comes looking. The kit's worth having.
Its owner comes looking, with friends.
The owner's dead in a wash. His poke and his map are still on him.
He's alive, with a broken leg. You splint it and he swears to repay you.
The tracks vanish on slickrock. Half a day lost.

ore_wagon_wreck.title: Ore Wagon Wreck
ore_wagon_wreck.text: A company ore wagon on its side in the wash, the driver dead in the traces. Nobody's come for the ore yet.

outcomes.text: Good heavy ore. The company won't miss a sack or two.
The company's guards ride up as you load the last sack.

0.text: {hero} gives the driver a proper service.

outcomes.text: A shallow grave and a wooden cross.

options.text: Report it at the next post.

outcomes.text: {hero} writes it up. The company pays a reward for its ore, and for honest folk.

wanted_poster.title: Wanted Poster
wanted_poster.text: A fresh poster on a fencepost: SNAKE-EYE PIKE, rides with Crane's crew. 200 CHIPS. LAST SEEN HEREABOUTS.

outcomes.text: You find Snake-Eye Pike watering his horse at a creek. He turns, slow.

1.text: Hey... that looks a lot like {hero}. {hero} laughs so hard the whole company joins in.

outcomes.text: It's Pike, all right. Mean eyes.
Hey... that looks a lot like {hero}. Nobody lets it go for days.
You ride on.

hanging_tree.title: The Hanging Tree
hanging_tree.text: Three of Crane's men have a homesteader on a horse under a cottonwood, a rope around his neck. "Keep riding, strangers."

outcomes.text: The hangman lets go of the rope and squares up to you.

text.bullseye: {hero}'s shot drops the hangman, and the second cuts the rope. The homesteader tumbles free and grabs your stirrup: "I'm with you."
text.hit: {hero} drops the hangman bleeding, and the homesteader wriggles free in the smoke: "I'm with you."
text.graze: {hero}'s shot only grazes the hangman, but in the smoke the homesteader slips the noose and runs for the trees.

outcomes.text: {hero} reads them the statute. They don't like it, but they ride off. The homesteader asks to come along.
"Law's a long way off." Guns come out.
Nobody looks back. Nobody forgets.

stagecoach.title: Stagecoach in Trouble
stagecoach.text: Gunfire ahead. A stagecoach is pinned down behind its own dead horses, and outlaws are working around the flanks.

outcomes.text: You hit them from behind.

options.text: Wait, then pick over what's left.

outcomes.text: By the time you ride down, it's over. The outlaws missed a strongbox under the seat.
The shooting fades behind you.

lone_wanderer.title: The Lone Wanderer
lone_wanderer.text: A lone rider waits at the crossroads, coat open, hand easy by the holster. "Heard your outfit's quick. Let's find out."

outcomes.text: You walk out into the crossroads. The wanderer smiles.

text.bullseye: {hero} shoots the pistol clean out of the wanderer's hand. The wanderer laughs, tips their hat and rides off. The company stands a little taller.
text.hit: {hero}'s shot clips the wanderer's gun arm. "Fair's fair," they say, and ride on.
text.graze: {hero}'s bullet tugs the wanderer's sleeve. A nod, and they're gone.
text.miss: {hero}'s shot goes wide. The wanderer holsters slowly, smiling, and rides away.

outcomes.text: The wanderer spits in the dust and rides off. Nobody says much for a while.
